hard_gates.name: official-native-openrouter-request-contract
hard_gates.evidence: Network-free request inspection proves the exact native endpoint, bearer header, strict response format, top-level provider routing, usage request, and router-metadata header.

hard_gates.name: upstream-failure-remains-diagnosable
hard_gates.evidence: A simulated upstream 401 preserves sanitized status, error message, request ID, generation ID, and router attempts without retaining the credential.

hard_gates.name: atomic-checkpoint-and-binding-safe-resume
hard_gates.evidence: Focused tests pass for per-call checkpoints, interruption, exact-binding resume, malformed bulk accounting, and failed sensitivity stopping.

hard_gates.name: live-provider-preflight
hard_gates.evidence: The clean no-call preflight matched exact model, endpoint, structured-output, context, and pricing metadata with no live failure.

hard_gates.name: paid-execution-remains-unauthorized
hard_gates.evidence: The three authorization locks remain closed and no provider inference occurred.

hard_gates.name: historical-results-preserved
hard_gates.evidence: Historical instruments and invalid results 002 and 003 remain unchanged, revoked, registered, and loadable.

decision.rationale: The native transport follows OpenRouter's official contract and preserves actionable sanitized upstream diagnostics while retaining the existing fail-closed execution and authorization boundaries.
limitations: No provider inference was made, so reviewer and dataset quality remain unknown.
The 120-case draft remains unfrozen and unopened for candidate evaluation.
No evidence-sufficiency implementation or release candidate is selected.
Live provider metadata must be refreshed within 24 hours immediately before any separately authorized execution.
